question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that it shall be the duty of the State to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historical interest?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 49**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 49** of the Indian Constitution falls under the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).**
 
• It states that it shall be the **duty of the State** to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historical interest.
 
• The article emphasizes the preservation of **India’s rich cultural heritage**.
 
• It is linked to ensuring the protection of **national monuments** from destruction, disfigurement, or removal.
 
• The implementation of this article is a responsibility of the government to ensure that **historical and cultural landmarks** remain intact for future generations.
 
• It is part of the broader framework of DPSPs, which aim to establish a welfare state and provide **guidance to governments** for achieving socio-economic goals.
 
• This article serves as the legal basis for various **heritage preservation initiatives** undertaken by the government, including the protection of UNESCO World Heritage sites in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 51**__

 __
 
• **Article 51** of the Indian Constitution is related to **international peace and security.**
 
• This article directs the State to promote **international law, treaty obligations,** and peaceful relations with other nations.
 
• It is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy** and focuses on fostering global cooperation and mutual respect.
 
 
 
• **Article 47**__
 __
 
• **Article 47** deals with the **duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition, standard of living, and public health.**
 
• It directs the State to prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs that are injurious to health.
 
• This article highlights the government's role in ensuring public health and welfare.
 
 
 
• **Article 45**__
 
 
• **Article 45** originally provided for free and compulsory education for children up to the age of 14 years.
 
• It was amended by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act (2002)** to make education a fundamental right under **Article 21A.**
 
• Now, Article 45 focuses on providing early childhood care and education for children below the age of six years.
